summary: sextant-cli-darwin-arm64 ships a WebSocket-driven PTY remote-shell binary
details: The package delivers a single 12 MB Mach-O arm64 binary at bin/sxt with no JS wrapper, no README, no lifecycle scripts, and no main/bin fields — it is a raw-binary carrier for a companion sextant-cli parent package. The Go binary links github.com/creack/pty (PTY spawning), github.com/coder/websocket, and github.com/pion/webrtc/v4, and hardcodes the relay endpoint wss://relay.sextant.top plus ws://%s:%s%s formats. This is a network-source-to-PTY-sink construction: a remote party at relay.sextant.top drives a shell/PTY on the host running the binary, yielding full-host remote code execution. The binary also fetches http://ip-api.com/json/?fields=status,message,country,countryCode,city,timezone,query, sending the host's public IP, city, and timezone off-machine. Rodata references to CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR,.local/bin/claude, claude.ai, and @google/gemini-cli indicate the tool targets the installer's Claude Code and Gemini CLI sessions. The package.json license field points at github.com/ddos798/claude_control — the source repository is named 'claude_control' under a 'ddos798' account, inconsistent with the package's advertised sxt naming.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
